title: Travels of Ibn Battuta
place: Tangier, Morocco, to Africa, Asia and Iberia
summary: The Moroccan scholar Ibn Battuta travelled across Africa, Asia and Iberia for nearly 30 years and later dictated his Rihla, which claims about 117,000 km of travel; scholars doubt some of the journeys it describes.
why: By his own account, he travelled farther than any other pre-modern explorer.

notes.problem: Source says modern scholars doubt several journeys; the distance rests on the Rihla alone, so it is not established.
